short: Duration-regulated seq2seq with toneme loss voices silent Mandarin EMG; gains rest on the auxiliary loss, not the architecture, and prompt grouping in the utterance split is unreported.
position: The paper changes two components of silent-EMG voicing: the timing map from EMG frames to audio frames (M06), now a duration predictor with a length regulator, and training-only supervision (M02), extended from phonemes to Mandarin tonemes [@li2022ssrnet]. Both are standard against the field: the duration-regulated model is rare but fails without the auxiliary loss, and auxiliary phonetic losses predate it [@toth2018multitask]. The headline result, 21.99% objective CER and a gain stated as 24.63% over the baseline (§IV-B.1), is confounded because the baseline [@gaddy2020digital] has no auxiliary loss. Tone itself changes CER by +6.51 in a single run (§IV-C.3), and no CER change in the paper says whether it is absolute or relative. The largest unaddressed risk is the split: five silent repetitions per prompt are divided 8:1:1 by utterance with no stated prompt grouping, so test sentences can occur in training. The results show in-speaker Mandarin voicing on read prompts, not tone-preserving silent speech in general.
